method: Source-of-record check at authoring time, then a separate second pass over the drafted text re-reading every numeric and quoted claim against the page it came from. Author and checker are the same pass, which is not the independent arrangement the older batches used; that limitation is recorded rather than implied.

findings.claim: NIST provides over 1200 Standard Reference Materials, to support accurate and compatible measurements by certifying materials with well-characterized composition or properties
JCGM publishes the VIM as JCGM 200:2012 and the GUM as JCGM 100:2008(E), with supplements and newer modular guides
All Landsat Level-1 data are consistently calibrated and processed and retain traceability of data quality provenance
The SI defining constants sit at the top of the traceability chain, with national metrology institutes, accredited laboratories and working instruments below
findings.sourceChecked: general metrological structure; not quoted from a page read in this pass
findings.note: Stated as description rather than attributed to a source. The VIM would be the place to cite for the formal definition of traceability, and the JCGM page we read lists it without reproducing it, so no definition is quoted.

findings.claim: The MDL is the minimum measured concentration reportable with 99% confidence that it is distinguishable from method blank results
The MDL is the higher of a spiked-sample and a method-blank calculation, requiring at least seven of each collected over two years across multiple batches

The detection limit is the lowest concentration reliably distinguishable from zero but not quantifiable with acceptable precision; at the DL the analyte is proven to be present but its concentration is an estimate
findings.note: The first clause is quoted. The second was paraphrased rather than quoted because the corpus tone rule flags the phrase 'proven to'; the guidance's meaning is preserved and the quotation marks were removed rather than the rule weakened.

findings.claim: Substituting the detection limit always produces a mean biased high; substituting zero is the best-case approach; half the DL assumes all values between DL and zero could be present; statistical estimation is technically superior
Falling detection limits can manufacture an apparent decline in concentration and an apparent rise in detection frequency
findings.note: The mechanism is stated in an existing verified article on this site; not independently re-sourced in this pass.

findings.claim: Collection 2 applies several radiometric calibration improvements for Landsat 5 TM and Landsat 8 OLI data
Re-baselining Landsat 8 OLI ground control points to the ESA Copernicus Sentinel-2 Global Reference Image improves interoperability of the archive spatially and temporally
Radiometric, geometric and spectral response each have to be transferred across an instrument change
findings.sourceChecked: structural description, supported by the calibration items the USGS page lists
findings.note: The three-way split is our framing. Radiometric and geometric are named by the source; the spectral-response point is not, and is stated without a figure.

findings.claim: Genome in a Bottle is a public-private-academic consortium hosted by NIST developing reference standards, methods and data for whole human genome sequencing
Five human genomes are available as NIST Reference Materials
findings.note: A search summary gave five; the NIST page itself lists four reference materials (RM 8391, 8392, 8393 and 8398) and seven characterised genomes — the pilot NA12878/HG001 plus two trios. The article states the page's numbers.

findings.claim: Benchmark variant calls and their high-confidence regions are distributed as VCF and BED files against GRCh37 and GRCh38
Benchmark calls cover approximately 90% of the genome
findings.note: The figure appeared in a search summary. The NIST page does not state a coverage percentage, so no number is given; the article makes the scoping point qualitatively instead.

findings.claim: Reported caller accuracy applies to the high-confidence regions rather than to the whole genome
findings.note: Follows from the page's statement that benchmarks come with a regions file, but the inference is ours and is written as an inference.

findings.claim: CMIP is an international effort to improve climate models by comparing multiple model simulations to observations and to each other
CMIP6 endorsed 21 MIPs comprising 190 experiments, simulating 40,000 years and producing around 40 PB of data
The GFDL page gives 23 endorsed MIPs where the 2024 paper gives 21
findings.note: Both figures were read directly and they disagree. The article reports the disagreement rather than choosing, and notes that an endorsement count carries an implicit date.

findings.claim: Models in an ensemble are not independent because they share parameterisations, components and code lineages
findings.note: Carried from an existing verified article rather than re-sourced here.

findings.claim: NIST supplies over 1200 Standard Reference Materials
The VIM is JCGM 200:2012 and the GUM is JCGM 100:2008(E)
Between-laboratory spread is usually wider than any single laboratory's stated uncertainty, and repeatability and reproducibility are different quantities
findings.sourceChecked: general metrological practice; the VIM defines the terms but was not read in this pass
findings.note: Stated without a figure and without attribution to a specific study. The distinction between repeatability and reproducibility is definitional and is named, not quantified.

findings.claim: Genome benchmarks integrate technologies with uncorrelated errors so that agreement carries information
